title: A deactivated term still dates new invoices for customers who keep it
custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • Scenario: Your shop switched off a term of its own, but a customer still on it has a work order ready to invoice.
  • You are an Admin user working at {Location-A}.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • Customer {Customer-A} holds the shop's own term {Term-A}, due 14 days after the invoice date, and {Term-A} is deactivated.
    For example: {Customer-A} is ZZAUTOTEST S7-06 Customer and {Term-A} is ZZAUTOTEST S7-06 Fourteen.
  • Work order {Work-order-1} for {Customer-A} is complete and ready to invoice (every part received, review done).
    For example: {Work-order-1} is S2-15442.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. Open {Work-order-1}'s Finance tab.
  2. Set Invoice Date to Oct 5, 2026.
  3. Click Create Invoice.
  4. Open the printed invoice.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: the invoice preview shows.
  • Step 2: the due date reads Oct 19, 2026 (Oct 5 + 14 days).
  • Step 3: the invoice is created.
  • Step 4: it shows the plain name {Term-A} (no "(Inactive)") and the due date Oct 19, 2026.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Credit terms", Confluence 963346440, version 3 (22 Oct 2026, "Renamed to Credit terms", Chris Ward), read 23 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11638, story SV-11674 (Story 5, New Customer and Edit Customer), story SV-11676 (Story 7, Due dates)

  • S7-E1: “A deactivated term still dates invoices and vendor invoices for the customers and vendors that keep it.”
  • S5-R8: “The customer card's "Credit term" shows "{name} (Inactive)" for a deactivated term. Invoices and printed documents show the plain name.”
